key_headlines.title: Government Launches 'Startup Boom' Initiative with 2 Trillion Won Fund
key_headlines.summary: The Korean government announced plans to designate 10 startup cities by 2030, with initial focus on Daejeon, Daegu, Gwangju, and Ulsan (home to major science and technology institutes). The initiative aims to create jobs and promote balanced regional development through specialized startup funds and support for local commerce zones.

key_headlines.title: South Korea's Q1 GDP Growth Surges to 1.7%, Highest in 5.5 Years
key_headlines.summary: Korea's first quarter real GDP grew 1.7% quarter-on-quarter, beating economist expectations of 0.9% and marking the strongest performance since Q3 2020. The growth was driven by semiconductor export strength and recovery in construction and equipment investment.

key_headlines.title: KOSDAQ Breaks 1,200 Mark for First Time in 25+ Years
key_headlines.summary: The KOSDAQ index surpassed the 1,200 level for the first time in over 25 years, driven by strong performance in semiconductor-related and biotech stocks. The broader market showed sectoral concentration, with power equipment and semiconductor shares recording historic highs.

key_headlines.title: Government Intensifies Regional Startup Policy to Address Youth Employment
key_headlines.summary: As part of the 'Everyone's Startup' initiative, the government is allocating 200 billion won in supplementary budget and plans to create specialized funds worth 2 trillion won through 2030. The policy emphasizes shifting from job-seeking to job-creation as a strategy to revitalize local economies and youth employment.

key_headlines.title: Meta Officially Announces 10% Workforce Reduction in May Amid AI Investment Costs
key_headlines.summary: Meta confirmed plans to lay off approximately 8,000 employees (10% of workforce) in May to offset massive AI investment expenditures, while also canceling 6,000 planned new hires. The move underscores the significant financial burden of AI development for tech giants.

sections.Hot Economy News: The Korean government has launched an ambitious 'startup boom' initiative targeting the creation of 10 startup cities by 2030, with a focus on balanced regional development and youth employment. Initial startup cities include Daejeon, Daegu, Gwangju, and Ulsan, with additional cities to be designated. The government plans to allocate 200 billion won in supplementary budget this year and establish 2 trillion won in specialized startup funds by 2030. Additionally, the government is promoting 'glocal' commercial zones and implementing job creation policies designed to transform the economy from job-seeking to job-creation. This comprehensive approach aims to establish a world-class startup ecosystem across Korea's regions.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's economy rebounded strongly in Q1 2026 with GDP growth of 1.7% quarter-on-quarter, exceeding expectations and marking the highest quarterly growth in 5.5 years. The robust growth was underpinned by semiconductor export strength, recovery in construction and equipment investment, and solid domestic demand. Financial institutions have begun raising their full-year growth forecasts, with some projecting growth rates reaching 2.4-3%. Government bond yields rose sharply following the GDP surprise announcement, with 3-year treasury yields climbing to 3.496%. The strong economic performance is expected to continue into Q2, though geopolitical tensions remain a key variable for the remainder of 2026.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean stock market showed mixed performance on April 24, with KOSPI trading near the 6,470 level amid lingering volatility and external pressures, while KOSDAQ achieved a historic milestone by surpassing the 1,200 mark for the first time in over 25 years. KOSPI has continued to set record highs for four consecutive trading sessions, though foreign investors conducted net selling exceeding 2 trillion won. The won-dollar exchange rate continued its upward trend due to elevated tensions between the United States and Iran around the Strait of Hormuz. Market sentiment remains cautious despite positive economic data, with geopolitical risks and rising global energy prices creating uncertainty.
sections.Industry & Technology: The semiconductor sector continues to lead market gains, with power equipment and semiconductor-related stocks recording historic highs amid strong global demand for semiconductors and energy infrastructure. Shipbuilding stocks also showed strong performance as global energy demand increases and ship replacement cycles align favorably, with companies like HD Hyundai Heavy Industries achieving record prices. However, the manufacturing sector faces headwinds as the yellow envelope law (union law amendments) has created escalating labor disputes between primary contractors and subcontractors, threatening small and medium-sized enterprises across steel, shipbuilding, and automotive sectors. According to recent data, over 1,000 unit unions have targeted 393 SME worksites since the law took effect on March 10.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's real estate market shows stark contrasts between small-unit apartments in prime areas and large units outside the capital region, with families strategically clustering their deposit points in Gangnam small apartments to achieve high jeonse bidding scores. A 44 square-meter apartment in Banpo recorded a maximum jeonse bidding score of 79 points, requiring families of 5-6 people to reside together in cramped 13-pyeong spaces, raising ethical concerns about housing policy fairness. Former housing minister Byun Chang-heum criticized private redevelopment projects for driving up housing prices and called for more inclusive housing policies centered on mid-rise, high-density development. Additionally, recent tax policy discussions suggest potential doubled capital gains taxes for single-home owners who provide jeonse arrangements, potentially accelerating tenant displacement.
sections.International Economy: The United States and Europe are raising tariff barriers against Chinese electric vehicles, while Korea's parallel 'K-IRA' industrial policy faces implementation challenges due to fiscal concerns from the Finance Ministry regarding tax revenue impacts. The U.S. Federal Reserve will hold its FOMC meeting next week amid ongoing discussions about interest rate policy, with Trump administration pressure for rate cuts creating tension with Fed officials asserting independence. The Philippines faced stagflation risks with simultaneous inflation and growth slowdown, prompting interest rate increases despite economic weakness. Global energy markets remain volatile due to Middle East tensions, with the U.S. deploying three aircraft carriers to the region for the first time since the Iraq War.
sections.AI & Economy: AI adoption is increasingly affecting labor markets, with youth and women being the first groups impacted as AI-exposed industries reduce employment, according to Bank of Korea research showing significant youth job losses in AI-intensive sectors. Meta officially confirmed plans to reduce its workforce by 10% (approximately 8,000 employees) in May to offset massive AI investment costs, while canceling 6,000 planned new hires, illustrating the financial burden AI development places on tech giants. OpenAI released its new GPT-5.5 model, described as the most intelligent and intuitive AI model to date, outperforming Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 across multiple performance benchmarks and intensifying competition in the generative AI market. Hanmi Global and Naver Cloud announced a strategic partnership to jointly pursue global data center projects, combining construction project management expertise with hyperscale AI technology capabilities. Hyundai Motor Group announced a 7.3 trillion won investment in the Bokjeong Station area to establish an AI and software technology hub for future mobility competition.
sections.Others: KB Kookmin Bank enhanced its non-face-to-face retirement pension service through KB Star Banking, improving customer experience with easier product verification and faster transaction processing, along with partnerships for real-time ETF consulting. The government's suggestion to reform local education funding has sparked strong pushback from the education sector, with the Korean Education Superintendents Council preparing official statements opposing the potential budget cuts. Cryptocurrency exchange Dunamu is expanding globally with executives attending high-profile meetings in Mar-a-Lago and accompanying South Korean leadership to Vietnam. Contrarian investor Michael Burry, previously skeptical of AI hype, has reversed course and began accumulating Microsoft and Adobe shares amid software replacement fears triggered by AI developments.
